headline: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement
standfirst: Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were…
body_markdown:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests. The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week. (The Guardian Asia)

**The Straits Times Asia** adds: MUMBAI, Oct 21 - An Indian court on Wednesday ordered the release of two \"cockroach\" movement leaders, local media reported, after they were detained last week for demonstrating at a historic protest venue in violation of a ban.

**The Hindu National** adds: Das and Ranka were released after the expiry of judicial custody in connection with the October 14 protest at Jantar Mantar.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by Times of India Top Stories, The Hindu National, The Guardian Asia and The Straits Times Asia. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
